tools.description: Expose live controls on a COMP: append custom parameters (sliders, toggles, menus, RGB, pulse) and bind them to node parameters so the artist can drive a generated system in real time. Point `comp_path` at a system container and list the controls; use each control's `bind_to` to wire it to one or more 'nodePath.parName' targets.

comp_path.description: COMP that will receive the custom parameters — usually a generated system's container.

page.description: Name of the custom-parameter page to add the controls to.

name.description: Control label; also sanitized into a valid TD custom-parameter name (e.g. 'blur amount' → 'Bluramount').

type.description: Widget kind: float/int sliders, a toggle, a dropdown menu, an RGB swatch, a momentary pulse, or a text field.

bind_to.description: Parameters this control should drive, each written as 'nodePath.parName' (e.g. '/project1/sys/blur1.size'). Each target is switched to expression mode so moving the control moves the parameter live. Not supported for 'rgb'/'pulse'.

tools.name: auto_ui_from_params
tools.description: Generate a performable control panel from an existing node/COMP's primitive parameters. It reads source_path, infers sliders/toggles/text fields, appends them as custom parameters on comp_path (default source_path), and optionally binds each control back to the source parameter. Use when a generated component has useful parameters but no playable UI yet.

source_path.description: Node or COMP whose parameters should become controls.

comp_path.description: COMP that receives the generated control panel. Defaults to source_path.

page.description: Custom-parameter page name for the controls.

parameters.description: Only expose these parameter names. Omit to infer useful primitive parameters.

max_controls.description: Maximum inferred controls when parameters is omitted.

bind.description: Bind generated controls back to source_path parameters.

tools.name: create_companion_surface
tools.description: Build a companion performance surface for an existing node/COMP: infer useful primitive parameters, add bound custom parameters, create a playable fader/cue panel, and optionally append a read-only preflight report. Use after generating a component that needs a human-facing control surface without hand-wiring every parameter.

source_path.description: Node or COMP whose useful parameters should be surfaced.

comp_path.description: COMP that receives the custom parameters and panel. Defaults to source_path.

name.description: Name of the playable panel container to build.

page.description: Custom-parameter page added by the auto UI pass.

parameters.description: Only expose these source parameter names. Omit to infer primitive controls.

max_controls.description: Maximum inferred controls when parameters is omitted.

include_faders.description: Build a playable fader/toggle surface for numeric inferred controls.

cue_buttons.description: Optional cue buttons to add to the playable surface.

cue.description: Name of a cue stored on the companion COMP.

label.description: Button label; defaults to the cue name.

morph_seconds.description: 0 = jump instantly to the cue; >0 = morph over this many seconds.

include_preflight.description: Append a read-only show_preflight_report result for the companion COMP.

bind.description: Bind generated custom parameters back to source_path parameters.

tools.name: create_control_surface
tools.description: Build a playable performance panel (a Container COMP of visual widgets) for live use, beyond the parameter dialog: vertical faders that drive parameters, and buttons that recall or morph to named cues (from manage_cue). Open the container in Perform/Panel mode for a touchable surface — faders move their parameters, cue buttons fire scenes (instantly or with a crossfade).

comp_path.description: Control COMP that holds the cues (manage_cue) and custom params. The surface is built inside it and its buttons fire that COMP's cues.

name.description: Name of the panel container to build.

align.description: How the panel lays out its widgets.

faders.description: Vertical faders, each driving a parameter.

param.description: Parameter the fader drives, written as 'nodePath.parName'.

label.description: Text shown above the fader; defaults to no label.

min.description: Value at the bottom of the fader.

max.description: Value at the top of the fader.

cue_buttons.description: Buttons that recall or morph to named cues.

cue.description: Name of a cue (stored with manage_cue) to fire.

label.description: Text shown on the button; defaults to the cue name.

morph_seconds.description: 0 = jump instantly to the cue; >0 = crossfade over this many seconds.

tools.name: animate_parameter
tools.description: Drive one or more node parameters over time with an LFO (sine/triangle/ramp/square/pulse/random). Creates an LFO CHOP and binds each target so it oscillates between min and max with the given period — movement without manual keyframing.

targets.description: Parameters to animate, each written as 'nodePath.parName' (e.g. '/project1/sys/blur1.size'). Each is switched to expression mode so it tracks the oscillator live.

waveform.description: Oscillator shape. Every waveform sweeps the full min–max range.

min.description: Low end of the value sweep.

max.description: High end of the value sweep.

period_seconds.description: Seconds for one full cycle (lower = faster).

container_path.description: Where to create the LFO CHOP; defaults to the first target's parent network.

tools.name: bind_to_channel
tools.description: Drive one or more node parameters from a CHOP channel by expression — the link that makes a visual react. Point it at an audio_features channel (bass/mid/treble/level) or a tempo_sync channel (ramp/pulse/beat) with a scale and offset, and each target parameter tracks that signal live. This is how you wire extract_audio_features / create_tempo_sync into a visual system. Optionally add attack/release smoothing (in seconds) — or a single `smooth` time — to insert a Lag CHOP between the channel and the parameter so reactivity follows a clean envelope instead of flickering on raw audio (e.g. a fast attack + slow release for a punchy hit that decays smoothly).

targets.description: Parameters to drive, each written as 'nodePath.parName' (e.g. '/project1/sys/transform1.scale'). Each is switched to expression mode so it tracks the channel live.

source_chop.description: Path of the CHOP that carries the driving channel (e.g. an audio_features Null).

channel.description: Channel name to read from the source CHOP (e.g. 'bass', 'level', 'ramp', 'pulse').

offset.description: Add to the scaled value (mapping offset).

attack.description: Smoothing rise time in seconds — how slowly the bound value follows the channel UP. 0 = instant (no smoothing on the way up). A small attack with a larger release gives a snappy hit that decays smoothly (envelope follow).

release.description: Smoothing fall time in seconds — how slowly the bound value follows the channel DOWN. 0 = instant (no smoothing on the way down). Set release > attack to remove flicker while keeping transients punchy.

smooth.description: Convenience: symmetric smoothing time in seconds applied to BOTH rise and fall (sets attack=release=smooth). Use this for simple low-pass-style de-jitter; use attack/release separately for an envelope follower.

smoothing_container.description: Where to create the Select+Lag smoothing CHOPs when smoothing is active; defaults to the first target's parent network. Ignored when no smoothing is requested.

tools.name: manage_presets
tools.description: Store, recall, list, or delete named snapshots of a COMP's parameter values — the live-performance preset system. Pair with create_control_panel: snapshot the knob positions and jump between looks. Snapshots are saved in the COMP's storage so they persist with the project.

action.description: store a snapshot, recall one, list all, or delete one.

comp_path.description: COMP whose parameter values the preset captures — usually a control-panel container.

params.description: Specific custom-parameter names to capture/restore. Defaults to every custom parameter on the COMP.

tools.name: manage_checkpoint
tools.description: Store / restore / list / delete a full snapshot of a sub-network — an 'undo point' to take before risky live edits. A checkpoint captures every node's constant parameters, the wiring, and node positions. Restoring reapplies parameters, recreates nodes that were deleted since (with their wiring), and prunes nodes that were created since. Unlike manage_presets (custom-parameter looks for performance), this captures the whole network for safe experimentation.

action.description: store a full snapshot of a sub-network, restore one, list all, or delete one. A checkpoint is an 'undo point' before risky live edits.

comp_path.description: Root COMP whose whole sub-network the checkpoint captures.

prune_created.description: (restore) Destroy nodes that were created after the checkpoint was stored.

recreate_deleted.description: (restore) Recreate nodes that were deleted after the checkpoint (type + params + wiring, best-effort).

tools.name: manage_cue
tools.description: Live-performance scene system: store / recall / morph / list / delete named cues (snapshots of a COMP's custom-parameter values). Unlike manage_presets, a cue can be reached with a timed `morph` that crossfades every numeric control from the current look to the cue over N seconds (eased), via a small Execute DAT — so you can glide between looks on stage instead of hard-cutting. Recall and morph also take an optional `quantize` ('beat'/'bar') that defers the change to the next musical boundary (from the project tempo) so scene changes land on the downbeat. Build cues with create_control_panel, then jump or morph between them.

action.description: store a cue (snapshot of the COMP's custom params), recall it instantly, morph to it over time, list, or delete.

comp_path.description: COMP whose custom-parameter values the cue captures (a control-panel container).

duration.description: (morph) Crossfade time in seconds from the current look to the cue.

quantize.description: (recall/morph) Snap the scene change to the music. 'off' (the default) fires immediately. 'beat' defers the recall/morph until the next beat boundary; 'bar' until the next bar (measure) boundary — read from the project tempo (op('/').time.tempo) and time signature. The change is scheduled, not blocking.

tools.name: manage_component
tools.description: Build a reusable component library by moving COMPs to/from .tox files on disk. 'save' uses a deferred, verified same-directory temporary export and refuses overwrite by default; set overwrite_policy='ask' for native Overwrite/Keep consent. 'load' keeps its legacy behavior and reads file_path into parent_path. Paths are on the machine running TouchDesigner.

action.description: save a COMP to a .tox file, or load a .tox into the project.

comp_path.description: (save) The COMP to save as a reusable .tox component.

parent_path.description: (load) COMP to place the loaded component inside.

linked.description: (load) Create a live-linked instance (externaltox) that re-reads the file on change, instead of an independent copy.

name.description: (load, linked) Name for the linked COMP; defaults to the file name.

create_folders.description: (save) Create the parent folders if they do not exist.

overwrite_policy.description: (save) Refuse an existing target, or ask through the native TouchDesigner broker before overwrite.

confirmation_timeout_ms.description: (save) Bounded wait for native overwrite consent.

operation_timeout_ms.description: (save) Bounded polling deadline for the deferred export job.

idempotency_key.description: (save) Opaque retry key for response-loss recovery.

tools.name: add_custom_parameters
tools.description: Transactionally add, edit, delete, sort, and organize a COMP's custom parameters through an authenticated structured TouchDesigner route. Legacy page+params calls remain valid. Supports Float, Int, Toggle, Str, Menu, Pulse, Header, OP, TOP, File, Folder, XYZW, RGBA, RGB, and XYZ; EXPRESSION and BIND are reversible and require TDMCP_RAW_PYTHON=on plus TDMCP_BRIDGE_ALLOW_EXEC=1 because their source is caller-supplied code. Constant and page-lifecycle operations remain available in restricted mode. EXPORT is explicitly HELD and returns an error without mutation. Built-ins are protected and failures roll back to the exact prior custom-page snapshot.

tools.name: scaffold_extension
tools.description: Give a COMP a Python extension class: create a Text DAT holding the class (with optional method stubs), wire it into an extension slot, optionally promote it (so members are callable directly on the COMP), and reinitialize. The other half of making a generated network reusable — pair with `add_custom_parameters` (knobs) and `manage_component` (save as .tox).

comp_path.description: The COMP to give a Python extension class.

class_name.description: Extension class name, e.g. 'WidgetExt' (capitalized to a valid identifier; must already be identifier-safe).

methods.description: Optional method-name stubs to add to the class (each takes only `self`).

promote.description: Promote the extension so its members are callable directly on the COMP (op.Method()).

slot.description: Extension slot (1–8) — a COMP can hold several extensions.

tools.name: create_macro
tools.description: Add one macro knob (a 0–1 custom parameter) to a COMP that drives many parameters at once, each remapped into its own [min,max] range with an optional response curve — a one-to-many control for sweeping a whole look from a single fader. Targets are bound by expression so they track the macro live.

comp_path.description: COMP that will hold the macro knob (usually a control-panel container).

min.description: Value this target takes when the macro is at 0.

max.description: Value this target takes when the macro is at 1.

curve.description: Response curve exponent: 1 = linear, >1 = ease-in, <1 = ease-out.

targets.description: Parameters this macro drives, each remapped from the macro's 0–1 into [min,max].

tools.name: randomize_controls
tools.description: Randomize a COMP's numeric custom parameters within their slider ranges — an instant new variation for live improvisation. `amount` blends toward random (1 = fully random, low values nudge the current look). Non-numeric controls (toggles, menus) are left untouched, so it is always safe to fire. Pair with manage_presets/manage_cue to snapshot a happy accident.

comp_path.description: COMP whose custom parameters to randomize (usually a control-panel container).

params.description: Specific custom-parameter names to randomize. Defaults to every numeric one.

amount.description: How far to move toward a random value in range: 1 = fully random, 0.2 = a gentle nudge from the current value. Lets you improvise without losing the current look.

seed.description: Optional RNG seed for repeatable results.

tools.name: create_phone_remote
tools.description: Serve a mobile-friendly web panel from a Web Server DAT so you can control a COMP's numeric custom parameters from a phone — just open the URL, no app to install. Each parameter becomes a touch slider that writes back live. SECURITY: like the bridge, this listens on all interfaces and accepts writes with no auth, so use it only on a trusted network. Pair with create_control_panel (the params to expose) and manage_cue (snapshot looks you dial in from the phone).

comp_path.description: Control COMP whose numeric custom parameters the phone page exposes.

port.description: TCP port for the remote web server (keep it distinct from the bridge's 9980).

tools.name: create_external_io
tools.description: Bridge TouchDesigner to the outside world: OSC/MIDI input (a control surface — bind incoming channels straight to parameters), OSC/MIDI output (send a CHOP's channels back out for bidirectional feedback to lighting desks, other apps or hardware — pass source_path), DMX/Art-Net output for lighting (dmx_out for any DMX desk; artnet_out for network Art-Net/sACN pixel-mapping of LED strips & stage fixtures), RTMP output to live-stream a TOP to Twitch/YouTube/OBS (rtmp_out — NVIDIA GPU on Windows only), or NDI / Syphon-Spout video input. To discover which channel a control sends (a 'MIDI learn'), wiggle it and read the input CHOP with get_td_nodes, then bind_to that channel. Validate live where possible, but real signal needs the hardware/sender present.

kind.description: What to bridge: OSC/MIDI/keyboard/gamepad/mouse input (a control surface — bind channels to parameters), OSC/MIDI output (send a CHOP's channels back out for bidirectional feedback — pass source_path), DMX/Art-Net output for lighting (dmx_out is the general DMX desk; artnet_out is a network-only Art-Net/sACN preset for pixel-mapping LED strips & stage fixtures — both send a CHOP's 0-255 channels and need source_path), RTMP output to live-stream a TOP to Twitch/YouTube/OBS-ingest (rtmp_out — pass source_path = the TOP to stream and url; needs an NVIDIA GPU on Windows), NDI / Syphon-Spout video input, or NDI / Syphon-Spout video output (ndi_out / syphon_spout_out — pass source_path = the TOP to send and an optional source_name for the NDI source / Spout sender name; flip active to start immediately). On Windows, Spout needs an NVIDIA or AMD GPU (no Intel).

parent_path.description: COMP to create the I/O operator in.

name.description: Name for the I/O operator; auto-generated when omitted.

port.description: (osc_in) UDP port to listen on / (osc_out) port to send to. Defaults to 7000.

normalize.description: (midi_in) How to scale incoming MIDI values.

bind_to.description: (osc_in/midi_in) Map incoming channels to parameters. Each binding tolerates a channel that hasn't arrived yet (falls back to 0 instead of erroring).

channel.description: Channel name produced by the input (e.g. an OSC address tail 'fader1', or a MIDI channel name).

source_path.description: (dmx_out/artnet_out/osc_out/midi_out) CHOP whose channel values are sent out, or (rtmp_out / video_device_out / ndi_out / syphon_spout_out) the TOP to send. Should live in the same COMP as parent_path so the wire/source connects.

interface.description: (dmx_out) DMX transport. (artnet_out forces a network protocol via `net`.)

net.description: (artnet_out) Network DMX protocol: Art-Net or sACN (streaming ACN). Defaults to Art-Net.

net_address.description: (dmx_out/artnet_out) Target IP address for Art-Net / sACN.

url.description: (rtmp_out) Full RTMP destination as {service url}/{stream key}, e.g. 'rtmp://live.twitch.tv/app/live_xxx'. If omitted but stream_key is given, prefix with rtmp_base.

rtmp_base.description: (rtmp_out) Ingest base URL to combine with stream_key when url is not given (defaults to YouTube's primary ingest).

stream_key.description: (rtmp_out) Stream key, appended to rtmp_base as '{rtmp_base}/{stream_key}'.

fps.description: (rtmp_out) Frame rate to stream at. Defaults to 30.

active.description: (rtmp_out/ndi_out/syphon_spout_out) Start sending immediately. Defaults off so the artist can confirm the destination/sender name first.

source_name.description: (ndi_in/syphon_spout_in/ndi_out/syphon_spout_out) Name of the NDI source or Spout sender to receive or send, or (video_device_out) the SDI/capture-card output device name. For outputs, defaults to the operator name when omitted.

tools.name: connect_companion_surface

A mapping table records label/address/target/mode/feedback for later editing.

parent_path.description: Parent COMP where the companion surface baseCOMP is created.

name.description: Name of the Companion OSC surface baseCOMP.

listen_port.description: Local OSC port for Companion/button input.

feedback_host.description: Remote host that receives outgoing OSC feedback.

feedback_port.description: Remote OSC port that receives outgoing feedback.

buttons.description: Button mappings to create as Select CHOP -> Null CHOP rows.

label.description: Human-readable button label for the mapping table.

address.description: Incoming OSC address for the button. If omitted, one is generated from the label.

target.description: Optional TouchDesigner target parameter, written as 'nodePath.parName'.

mode.description: How the incoming button channel should drive the target parameter.

feedback_channel.description: Optional outgoing OSC feedback channel name for this button.

create_mapping_dat.description: Create/populate a tableDAT listing label, address, target, mode, and feedback.

tools.name: duplicate_network
tools.description: Copy a node or whole COMP (and all its contents) to a new node, placed in the source's parent or another parent_path. Returns the source path and the new copy's path. Use duplicate this way to clone a built network; use create_container instead when you just need a fresh empty COMP.

source_path.description: Path of the node/COMP to duplicate.

name.description: Name for the copy (auto-generated if omitted).

parent_path.description: Where to place the copy (defaults to the source's parent).

tools.name: arrange_network
tools.description: Tidy an existing network into a readable left→right data-flow layout, or use layout_mode=explicit for one bounded, atomic exact-coordinate mutation with stale-context checks, readback and rollback. Annotation-aware automatic layout remains available, and omission of layout_mode preserves the legacy response. It never adds, deletes, or rewires nodes.

path.description: COMP whose children to arrange, e.g. '/project1' or a container path.

recursive.description: Also arrange the nodes inside nested COMPs (each network is tidied on its own).

include_docked.description: Move each node's docked DATs (e.g. GLSL *_pixel or callbacks DATs) with it by the same delta, like an interactive drag. Set false to reposition only the nodes themselves.

annotation_aware.description: Treat each annotation and the operators it encloses as one layout unit. Uses structured bridge routes and never raw Python.

resize_annotations.description: With annotation_aware, resize non-empty annotation bounds to the enclosed content plus annotation_padding.

annotation_padding.description: Padding in network-editor units when resize_annotations is enabled.

layout_mode.description: Keep automatic layout by default, or place exact coordinates atomically.

positions.description: Explicit mode only: normalized absolute child path to exact [x, y] coordinates.

target_source.description: Explicit mode only: use the supplied paths or compare them with active selection.

idempotency_key.description: Explicit mode only: stable response-loss recovery key.

tools.name: manage_artist_workspace
tools.description: Open, inspect, restore, or cancel one bounded TouchDesigner editor workspace using an existing Network Editor plus one right-hand TOP Viewer or Panel split. The bridge schedules every UI access on the TD main thread, keeps only JSON job state, uses compare-and-swap restoration, and fails closed in Perform/headless/conflicted states. It never opens arbitrary UI, creates project operators, adds graph undo, or falls back to raw Python; the authenticated structured routes work with ALLOW_EXEC=0.

network_path.description: Explicit COMP to show in the existing Network Editor.

viewer_path.description: Exact TOP output or panel-capable COMP to show.

viewer_mode.description: Use a bounded TOP Viewer or Panel pane; arbitrary pane types are not accepted.

split_ratio.description: Share of the existing Network Editor after the right-hand split.

lease_seconds.description: Bounded lease before compare-and-swap cleanup is attempted.

tools.name: create_panic
tools.description: Build a live-performance safety control — the 'oh no' button every VJ needs. Wraps a source in a small COMP with two instant kill switches: Blackout forces the output to black (a Level TOP's brightness1 driven to 0) and Freeze holds the last frame (a Cache TOP stops capturing, active → 0). With an input_path the source is pulled in by a Select TOP (so it can live in another container); without one a built-in Ramp TOP test source is used so it builds and previews standalone. Output is a Null TOP. Big Blackout / Freeze toggle buttons are exposed on the container so a performer can hit them instantly. Marked destructive because firing Blackout/Freeze disables the live output. Returns the container, the source/freeze/blackout/output node paths, and the initial toggle states.

input_path.description: Optional absolute path of the live source TOP to protect. Pulled in via a Select TOP (TD wires can't cross containers, so it's referenced by path). If omitted, a built-in test source (Ramp TOP) is used so the panic COMP still builds and previews on its own.

blackout.description: Initial Blackout state. When on, the output is forced to black (Level TOP brightness1 = 0) — the instant kill switch.

freeze.description: Initial Freeze state. When on, the last frame is held instead of passing the live input (Cache TOP stops capturing — active = 0).

expose_controls.description: Expose big Blackout and Freeze toggle buttons on the container so a performer can hit them instantly.

parent_path.description: Parent COMP the panic container is built inside (default '/project1').

tools.name: create_clip_launcher
tools.description: Build an Ableton-style clip launcher: a grid panel (Container COMP) of clip buttons, one per named cue (from manage_cue), for fast hands-on scene switching during a live set. Open the container in Perform/Panel mode and tap a clip to fire its cue — instantly, or (with morph_time) crossfading to it over N seconds (eased, the same engine manage_cue uses). Store the cues with manage_cue / create_control_panel first.

comp_path.description: Control COMP that holds the cues (manage_cue) and custom params. The launcher panel is built inside it and its buttons fire that COMP's cues.

name.description: Name of the launcher panel container to build.

cues.description: Cue names (stored with manage_cue) to lay out in the grid, in order. Each becomes a clip button labelled with its cue name.

rows.description: Grid row count. Defaults so rows*cols covers all cues (derived from cues length).

cols.description: Grid column count. Defaults to ceil(sqrt(cues)) when omitted (derived from cues length).

morph_time.description: 0 = each button jumps instantly to its cue; >0 = every button crossfades to its cue over this many seconds (eased morph, same engine as manage_cue).

tools.name: clip_audio_transport
tools.description: Create a synchronized clip transport container: a Movie File In TOP video lane, optional Audio File In CHOP lane, Null outputs, deterministic layout, and Play/Loop/Speed controls bound across both lanes. Use it as a reusable building block before clip launchers, VJ decks, or stream/output chains.

parent_path.description: Parent COMP path where the transport container is created.

name.description: Name of the transport container COMP to create.

movie_file.description: Optional movie file path for the Movie File In TOP.

audio_file.description: Optional audio file path for the Audio File In CHOP.

include_audio.description: Create an Audio File In CHOP transport lane alongside the movie lane.

autoplay.description: Initial play state for movie/audio file inputs.

loop.description: Initial loop state for movie/audio file inputs.

speed.description: Initial playback speed. Negative values reverse where the operator supports it.

expose_controls.description: Expose Play, Loop and Speed custom parameters on the transport container.

tools.name: osc_router_matrix
tools.description: Create an offline-safe OSC control matrix: one Constant CHOP plus OSC Out CHOP per target, deterministic left-to-right layout, target-specific address prefixes, and a structured report of every emitted OSC address. Use it as the primitive for QLab, atemOSC/Companion, Resolume, VDMX, or any OSC-speaking show-control endpoint.

parent_path.description: Parent COMP to build the router in.

name.description: Name of the router container COMP.

address.description: OSC address or address tail. A leading slash is optional.

channel.description: Optional local Constant CHOP channel name. Defaults from the address tail.

label.description: Human label stored in the returned route report.

default.description: Initial value sent for this route.

routes.description: Routes/channels to create for every target.

name.description: Target label and node suffix, e.g. qlab, resolume, atem.

prefix.description: Optional prefix prepended to every route address for this target.

active.description: Start the OSC Out CHOP active immediately.

targets.description: OSC destinations. Each target gets a Constant CHOP and OSC Out CHOP.

tools.name: qlab_osc_bridge
tools.description: Create a QLab OSC control bridge using the OSC router matrix primitive. It exposes /go, /stop, /panic, /pause, /resume, /reset and optional /cue/{number}/start routes to QLab's configurable OSC receive port, without requiring QLab to be running during build.

parent_path.description: Parent COMP to build the QLab OSC bridge in.

name.description: Name of the bridge container COMP.

cue_numbers.description: Optional QLab cue numbers to expose as /cue/{number}/start routes.

tools.name: atem_switcher_control
tools.description: Create an OSC control preset for an ATEM switcher routed through atemOSC, Bitfocus Companion, or another OSC relay. This does not use the Blackmagic SDK directly; it builds an offline-safe TouchDesigner OSC matrix for cut/auto/FTB and program/preview input selection.

parent_path.description: Parent COMP to build the ATEM control preset in.

name.description: Name of the ATEM control container COMP.

host.description: atemOSC, Companion, or OSC relay host/IP.

tools.name: resolume_vdmx_output_chain
tools.description: Create an OSC control chain for driving Resolume, VDMX, or both from TouchDesigner. It builds target-specific OSC Out lanes with layer opacity, crossfader, speed, clip trigger, and blackout channels; use it beside video/NDI/Syphon output tools when an external VJ app handles playback or final compositing.

parent_path.description: Parent COMP to build the Resolume/VDMX control chain in.

name.description: Name of the output-control container COMP.

target.description: Which OSC target preset(s) to create.

tools.name: obs_stream_control
tools.description: Create an OBS WebSocket v5 control rig in TouchDesigner: websocketDAT connection, Constant CHOP command channels for stream/record/scene actions, and a chopExecute DAT that dispatches op:6 request payloads such as StartStream, StopStream, ToggleStream, StartRecord, StopRecord, ToggleRecord, and SetCurrentProgramScene. tdmcp never accepts or stores OBS passwords; if OBS authentication is enabled, complete Identify authentication manually in the generated obs_dispatch DAT.

parent_path.description: Parent COMP to build the OBS control rig in.

auto_connect.description: Start the websocketDAT active immediately. Defaults false for show safety.

include_recording.description: Also create StartRecord, StopRecord, and ToggleRecord controls.

scenes.description: Optional OBS scene names. Each creates a scene_* control that sends SetCurrentProgramScene.

auth_required.description: Set true only as a reminder that OBS WebSocket authentication must be completed manually; tdmcp never stores an OBS password.

tools.name: notch_touchengine_bridge
tools.description: Build a guarded Notch TOP or Engine COMP/TouchEngine bridge scaffold with notes, output, and optional Notch play/speed controls. This does not validate a Notch license or target runtime; live validation remains explicit.

parent_path.description: Parent COMP path to build inside.

mode.description: Create a Notch TOP bridge or an Engine COMP TouchEngine bridge.

width.description: Notch TOP or placeholder output width. Ignored by mode=engine_comp.

height.description: Notch TOP or placeholder output height. Ignored by mode=engine_comp.

active.description: Start the Notch TOP active. Ignored by mode=engine_comp.

expose_controls.description: Expose Play and Speed controls where possible.

tools.name: create_decks
tools.description: Build a DJ-style VJ mixer. Without decks[], it preserves the legacy A/B Cross TOP mixer with GainA/GainB controls. With decks[], it builds a 2-8 deck mixer: every deck pulls a source TOP (or a test source) through gain and FX-send Level TOPs, decks 3+ blend into a running Cross TOP chain, a Switch TOP provides hard transition cuts, a final Cross TOP blends program vs cut, and an additive FX-send bus returns per-deck sends into the master. Output is a Null ready for post-processing or setup_output.

deck_a.description: Absolute path of the source TOP for deck A (pulled in via a Select TOP, so it can live in another container). If omitted, a built-in test source (Noise TOP) is created so the mixer builds standalone.

deck_b.description: Absolute path of the source TOP for deck B (pulled in via a Select TOP). If omitted, a built-in test source (Ramp TOP) is created so the mixer builds standalone.

crossfade.description: Master crossfader position: 0 = full deck A, 1 = full deck B, 0.5 = even blend.

decks.description: Optional N-channel deck list. When supplied, create_decks builds a 2-8 deck mixer with per-deck gain, FX sends, a running blend chain, and a hard-cut switch bus.

name.description: Human label for this deck, used in exposed controls and structured output.

source.description: Absolute path of the source TOP for this deck. If omitted, a built-in test source is created.

gain.description: Initial per-deck gain/brightness, exposed as a live control when enabled.

fx_send.description: Initial per-deck send amount into the additive FX-send bus.

mix.description: For deck 3 and later, the initial blend amount into the running program mix. Decks 1-2 use crossfade.

cut_deck.description: Zero-based deck index selected by the hard transition-cut bus in N-channel mode.

cut_mix.description: Blend between the continuous program mix and the hard transition-cut bus: 0 = program mix, 1 = cut bus.

expose_controls.description: Expose live 'Crossfader' + per-deck 'GainA'/'GainB' knobs on the container so the mix is playable on arrival.

parent_path.description: Parent COMP the mixer container is built inside (default '/project1').

tools.name: learn_control
tools.description: EXPERIMENTAL two-step 'MIDI learn'. Call once with mode:'snapshot' (controls at rest) to record every channel of an input CHOP (a midiin/oscin CHOP or a Null fed by one); then wiggle one hardware knob/fader and call again with mode:'bind' — it diffs against the snapshot, finds the channel that moved the most, and binds your target parameter to it by expression (with optional scale/offset). The snapshot is kept in the parent COMP's storage between the two calls. This is live/stateful: verify the matched channel in the report.

mode.description: snapshot: record the current value of every channel of source_chop. bind: re-read source_chop, find the channel that moved the most since the snapshot, and bind target to it. Call snapshot first (controls at rest), wiggle one hardware control, then call bind.

source_chop.description: Absolute path of the input CHOP carrying the hardware controls (e.g. a midiin/oscin CHOP or a Null fed by one).

target.description: Parameter to drive, written as 'nodePath.parName' (e.g. '/project1/sys/transform1.scale'). Required for mode:'bind'; switched to expression mode so it tracks the matched channel live.

scale.description: Multiply the matched channel value (mapping gain).

offset.description: Add to the scaled value (mapping offset).

min_delta.description: mode:'bind' minimum NORMALIZED movement (default 0.05). The winning channel's delta is normalized by max(|old|, |new|, epsilon) — a unit-free relative change — so a 0–127 MIDI CC and a 0–1 OSC float compare fairly. If the top channel moved less than this, nothing is bound and you're told to wiggle the control harder. Raise it to reject controller jitter; lower it for very small/slow knobs.

parent_path.description: COMP whose storage persists the snapshot between the snapshot and bind calls (defaults to /project1).

tools.name: scaffold_vj_deck
tools.description: Compose a complete, playable VJ deck UI in one call: it builds a DJ-style A/B deck mixer (create_decks) with a crossfader, adds an on-screen fader control surface (create_control_surface) with crossfade + per-deck gain faders, and creates a midiinCHOP control surface (create_external_io) whose channels are bound to the same crossfader/gain parameters for hands-on MIDI control. Pass deck_a/deck_b source TOP paths (or omit for test sources), and an optional midi_map of channel→control bindings (defaults to ch1c1→crossfader, ch1c2→gain_a, ch1c3→gain_b). This is the deck-scaffold layer on top of the create_decks primitive — it wires the existing deck, surface, and I/O tools into one UI container.

name.description: Base name for the VJ-deck container COMP.

parent_path.description: COMP the VJ deck is scaffolded inside (default '/project1').

deck_a.description: Absolute path of the source TOP for deck A. If omitted, a built-in test source is created.

deck_b.description: Absolute path of the source TOP for deck B. If omitted, a built-in test source is created.

crossfade.description: Initial crossfader position: 0 = full deck A, 1 = full deck B.

midi.description: Create a midiinCHOP control surface and bind its channels to the deck controls (MIDI-mappable VJ deck).

midi_map.description: Explicit MIDI channel → control bindings. When omitted, a sensible default map (ch1c1→crossfader, ch1c2→gain_a, ch1c3→gain_b) is used.

channel.description: MIDI input channel name (e.g. 'ch1c7') that this control listens to. Wiggle the control and read the midiinCHOP to learn it.

control.description: Which VJ-deck control this MIDI channel drives.

faders.description: Add an on-screen fader control surface (crossfader + per-deck gain faders) inside the container.

tools.name: create_synesthesia_unreal_osc
tools.description: Build a named OSC-out preset map for driving Synesthesia or Unreal Engine from TouchDesigner. Picks a preset ('synesthesia' → prefix '/syn', port 6448; 'unreal' → prefix '/unreal', port 8000), builds a Constant CHOP with one named channel per control (channel name = '<prefix>/<control>' so an oscoutCHOP emits the exact address the target app expects), and wires it into an oscoutCHOP aimed at host:port. Override the control names, prefix, host, or port as needed. This is the preset layer on top of create_external_io osc_out — it fills in the address templates and default control set so the send 'just works' with the target app. Bind audio/analysis to the source channels (e.g. op('controls')['syn/Bass']) to make the receiving app react.

name.description: Base name for the container COMP.

parent_path.description: COMP to create the OSC-out chain in (default '/project1').

preset.description: Named OSC-out preset — sets the address prefix, default port, and default control names for Synesthesia or Unreal Engine.

host.description: Destination IP the OSC messages are sent to (the machine running Synesthesia / Unreal).

port.description: UDP port to send OSC to. Null uses the preset's default (Synesthesia 6448, Unreal 8000).

controls.description: Override the preset's control names. Each becomes an OSC address '/<prefix>/<name>' and a channel on the source Constant CHOP you drive/bind.

prefix.description: Override the preset's OSC address prefix (the part before the control name). Null uses the preset default (syn / unreal).

active.description: Start sending immediately. Defaults off so you can confirm the destination host/port first.

tools.name: create_cue_sequencer
tools.description: Build a bar-quantized cue timeline: a Beat CHOP (on the global tempo) + a CHOP Execute DAT that, on each bar (or beat) boundary, advances through an ordered list of steps and recalls — or morphs over morph_seconds — that step's cue on a target COMP. The deterministic, musically-timed counterpart to create_autopilot (which is random/cyclic). Reuses manage_cue's stored cues and the same cue_morph engine, so store the target's cues with manage_cue first. Live Active / Step / BarsPerStep controls let you pause, jump, or retune on stage.

target.description: COMP whose stored cues (tdmcp_cues, from manage_cue) the sequencer recalls/morphs. Store the cues first.

cue.description: Name of a cue (stored on the target with manage_cue) to fire.

bars.description: How many quantize units (bars or beats) this step holds before advancing.

steps.description: The ordered timeline: each step names a cue and how many bars/beats it holds before the next.

loop.description: When the last step finishes, wrap back to the first (true) or stop (false).

quantize.description: Unit each step's count is measured in: 'bar' (× the project's beats-per-bar) or raw 'beat'.

morph_seconds.description: 0 = snap to each cue instantly on its boundary; >0 = crossfade to it over this many seconds (via the same cue_morph engine manage_cue uses).

name.description: Name of the engine container built inside target.

parent_path.description: Where to create the sequencer engine COMP.

tools.name: create_stage_dashboard
tools.description: Serve one unified live-performance cockpit from a Web Server DAT — a single responsive web page (phone + laptop) that combines a grid of cue-launch buttons (recall named cues from manage_cue on the target COMP), master faders bound to chosen parameters, a big PANIC button (toggles the target COMP's Blackout/Freeze safety pars, the create_panic mechanism), and a live readout strip (a beat indicator plus a VU bar reading an audio-features Null CHOP). Open the URL — no app to install — and the page POSTs every control change back to the server, which applies it. SECURITY: like the bridge and create_phone_remote, this listens on all interfaces and accepts writes with NO auth, so use it only on a trusted network. Store cues with manage_cue, expose params with create_control_panel, and run create_panic first so the Blackout/Freeze toggles exist.

target.description: Control COMP the dashboard is built inside. It holds the cues (manage_cue) and the Blackout/Freeze toggles (create_panic); cue buttons fire that COMP's cues and the panic button toggles its safety pars.

port.description: TCP port for the dashboard web server (keep it distinct from the bridge's 9980 and phone_remote's 9981).

cues.description: Cue names (stored with manage_cue) to expose as launch buttons, in order. Each becomes a button that instantly recalls its cue on the target COMP. Empty omits the cue grid.

faders.description: Master faders, each a { label, par_path } that becomes a slider writing the parameter live. Empty omits the fader bank.

label.description: Fader label shown on the page.

par_path.description: Absolute parameter path the fader drives, e.g. '/project1/level1/brightness1' or '/project1/comp1/Intensity'. Written live as a float.

audio_features.description: Optional audio-features Null CHOP path for the readout strip's VU bar (first channel). When omitted the readout still renders (beat from the timeline, VU flat).

name.description: Name of the Web Server DAT (and its callbacks DAT) built inside the target COMP.

layout.description: Dashboard layout. 'v1' is the original (cues + faders + readout + panic). 'v2' adds stereo VU, BPM, cue timeline strip, FPS/cook overlay, and a sticky confirm-PANIC bar. Default 'v1' for backward compat.

tempo_channel.description: v2 only. Absolute path to a CHOP whose first channel is current BPM (e.g. a detect_tempo Null CHOP). Omitted = BPM widget hidden.

cue_times.description: v2 only. Cue start times (seconds from show start) from compose_cue_list, for the timeline strip's playhead. Empty = strip omitted, cue grid still shown.

tools.name: create_palette
tools.description: Generate a reusable colour palette + gradient other tools can bind to. In 'harmony' mode it computes N swatches from a base hue and a colour-theory rule (complementary / analogous / triad / tetrad / monochrome); in 'from_source' mode it samples dominant colours from a source TOP. It builds a Ramp TOP gradient (key colours from a docked Table DAT) plus a Constant CHOP exposing each swatch as swatch{i}r/g/b channels — feed those into create_color_grade, generate_from_moodboard or bind_to_channel. Live BaseHue / Saturation / Value / Rule / Count controls are exposed on the parent. Builds standalone (a harmony palette needs no source).

mode.description: How swatches are derived: 'harmony' computes them from a base hue + a colour-theory rule (pure maths); 'from_source' samples dominant colours from a source TOP.

base_hue.description: (harmony) Base hue on the colour wheel, 0..1 (0 = red, 0.333 = green, 0.666 = blue).

rule.description: (harmony) Colour-theory spread: complementary (base + opposite), analogous (neighbours), triad (3 evenly spaced), tetrad (4 evenly spaced), monochrome (one hue, varied brightness).

count.description: Number of swatches to produce (1..13; capped because the swatch Constant CHOP holds 40 channels = 13 RGB swatches).

analogous_spread.description: (harmony, analogous rule) Hue step between neighbours, 0..0.5 (0.083 ≈ 30°).

source.description: (from_source) Absolute path of a TOP to sample dominant colours from. It is down-res'd to a tiny image and its pixels are read back; if missing/unreadable the palette falls back to a neutral greyscale ramp.

parent_path.description: COMP to build the Ramp TOP + swatch CHOP inside.

name.description: Base name for the created nodes.

expose_controls.description: Add BaseHue / Saturation / Value / Rule / Count custom parameters to parent_path.

tools.name: create_data_source
tools.description: Ingest live external data onto a binding-ready channel/table — the input counterpart to create_data_visualization and bind_to_channel. 'json'/'csv' poll a URL with a Web Client DAT (and cook from a static sample of `fields` when no url is given, so it works offline); 'osc' listens on a UDP port; 'serial' reads a device. Numeric `fields` become channels on an output Null CHOP (named for each key) so other tools can bind to them; the raw text is exposed on a Null DAT. Live OSC/serial values only appear when a sender/device is present.

kind.description: Where the data comes from: 'json' or 'csv' poll a URL with a Web Client DAT (or, with no url, cook from a static sample so it works offline), 'osc' listens for OSC messages on a UDP port, 'serial' reads a serial device. json/csv always cook; osc/serial only carry values once a sender/device is present.

parent_path.description: COMP to build the data source inside.

name.description: Base name for the created sub-network.

url.description: (json/csv) Endpoint the Web Client DAT fetches. When omitted the network still cooks from a static sample so other tools have channels to bind to.

port.description: (osc) UDP port to listen on. Defaults to 7000.

device.description: (serial) Serial port, e.g. 'COM3' on Windows or '/dev/tty.usbserial' on macOS.

fields.description: Numeric keys to extract. Each becomes a channel on the output Null CHOP (named for the key) so create_data_visualization / bind_to_channel can bind to it, and a column in the offline sample table.

poll_seconds.description: (json/csv) How often the Web Client DAT re-fetches the URL.

expose_controls.description: Surface live 'Active' and 'Poll' controls on the source operator.

tools.name: create_led_mapper
tools.description: Build a pixel-mapping chain from a source TOP to an LED fixture grid and DMX Out CHOP over Art-Net or sACN. The generated network resizes to width×height, samples one texel per fixture pixel, preserves RGB channels, and returns created node paths, channel count, warnings, and live Brightness/Universe controls on the parent COMP. It defaults to a moving Ramp test source so the chain can cook without input; real network output still requires a reachable fixture/node and should be verified before sending. Use create_dmx_fixture_pipeline for fixture patching and this tool when you specifically need image-to-pixel mapping.

source.description: TOP path whose image is mapped to the fixtures. If omitted, a built-in moving Ramp TOP test source is created so the chain cooks with no input.

width.description: Pixels per row (columns). Each texel of the WxH grid drives one LED fixture.

height.description: Rows of pixels. 1 = a single LED strip.

layout.description: Pixel wiring order along the strip/grid: horizontal (rows left-to-right), vertical (columns), or serpentine (alternate rows reversed — boustrophedon strips).

start_universe.description: Art-Net / sACN universe of the first pixel.

start_channel.description: DMX start channel (1-512) of the first pixel within the starting universe.

net.description: Network DMX protocol: Art-Net or sACN (streaming ACN).

net_address.description: Target IP address for Art-Net / sACN. Defaults to the operator's own default.

fps.description: Output frame rate (DMX Out CHOP sample rate).

parent_path.description: COMP to build the pixel-map chain in.

name.description: Base name for the created nodes.

tools.name: batch_operations
tools.description: Run an ordered list of create / connect / setParam operations in one call (fail-forward, per-operation warnings; not transactional). Exposes the network builder as a general primitive — distinct from set_parameters_batch, which only sets parameters. Names created earlier can be referenced by later connect/setParam operations.

default_parent.description: Parent path for `create` operations that omit `parent_path`.

name.description: Optional name for the new node; later operations in this batch can reference it (TD may adjust it to avoid collisions).

parent_path.description: Parent to create this node inside; defaults to `default_parent`.

parameters.description: Initial parameters to set on the new node, e.g. { period: 2, amplitude: 0.5 }.

from.description: Source node — a name created earlier in this batch, or an absolute path (e.g. '/project1/noise1').

to.description: Target node — a name created earlier in this batch, or an absolute path (e.g. '/project1/level1').

from_output.description: Output connector index on the source node (default 0).

to_input.description: Input connector index on the target node (default 0).

path.description: Node to update — a name created earlier in this batch, or an absolute path. Names are resolved to their created paths.

parameters.description: Parameters to set on the node, e.g. { period: 2, amplitude: 0.5 }.

operations.description: Ordered list of create / connect / setParam operations. Runs in order, fail-forward: a failing operation becomes a warning and the rest still run (not transactional). Names created earlier can be referenced by later connect/setParam operations.

tools.name: manage_annotation
tools.description: Self-document a network: create a titled annotation box; safely edit an existing Annotate COMP's title, body, RGBA background, or exact node-space bounds; set an op comment; list annotations; or inspect geometric enclosure. The edit action is a structured, verified transaction that works with raw Python disabled.

action.description: 'create' a titled annotation box, 'edit' an Annotate COMP's text/style/bounds, 'comment' to set an op's comment, 'list' the annotations in a network, or 'enclosed' to list the ops a box geometrically encloses.

parent_path.description: (create/list) The network (COMP) to act in.

text.description: (create) The title/text shown on the box; (comment) the comment string to set.

name.description: (create) Name for the annotation COMP (defaults to 'anno').

node_path.description: (comment) The op to comment on; (enclosed) the annotation box whose enclosed ops to list.

x.description: (create) Node-space X position for the box's left edge.

y.description: (create) Node-space Y position for the box's top edge.

title.description: (edit) Exact Annotate COMP title; empty clears it.

body.description: (edit) Exact Annotate COMP body; empty clears it.

color.description: (edit) Exact RGBA background colour, four channels from 0 to 1.

tools.name: set_perform_mode
tools.description: Toggle perform mode — the one switch the artist flips before going live. When enabled, tdmcp stores an advisory flag that tools can read before doing nonessential compute; the built-in guard currently suppresses auto preview captures. The flag is stored on the TD root op (op('/').store('tdmcp_perform_mode', ...)). Advisory: this does not stop the TD timeline or kill audio/video processing. Call with enabled=false after the show to resume normal operation.

enabled.description: true to enter perform mode before a live show, false to leave it afterward. While perform mode is ON, tools that honor the advisory flag skip nonessential compute. The built-in guard currently suppresses auto preview captures; future tools can opt in by checking op('/').fetch('tdmcp_perform_mode', False) before doing expensive work. It does NOT stop the TD timeline or kill audio/video processing.

tools.name: bind_audio_reactive
tools.description: Make a whole COMP react to the music in one call — the core VJ move. Point `target` at a COMP with numeric custom-parameter knobs and `source_chop` at an audio-feature CHOP (e.g. an extract_audio_features Null carrying level/bass/mid/treble), and each knob is switched to expression mode tracking an audio band. Omit `mappings` to auto-map knobs by name heuristic (bright/level/opacity→level, scale/size/zoom→bass, hue/color→treble, speed/rate/rot→mid; unrecognized knobs are skipped), or pass explicit param→channel bindings with per-binding scale/offset. By default appends a master 'Reactivity' float knob (0–2, default = intensity) that scales every binding so the artist can dial the whole network's reactivity from one control. Fail-forward: a missing source CHOP, an absent channel, or an already-bound parameter are warnings, not failures — only a missing/non-COMP target is fatal. This tool only WIRES an existing COMP to an existing CHOP, building no nodes: produce the feature CHOP with extract_audio_features (or create_spectrum) first, use create_audio_reactive when you want a whole new reactive network with its own visual, and bind_to_channel for finer single-parameter control.

target.description: COMP whose numeric custom parameters (knobs) should react to the music.

source_chop.description: CHOP carrying audio feature channels (e.g. an extract_audio_features Null). Expected channels: level, bass, mid, treble.

intensity.description: Master reactivity amount (0=off, 1=normal, 2=strong) — scales every binding.

mappings.description: Explicit param→channel bindings. Omit to auto-map the target COMP's numeric custom parameters by name heuristics.

param.description: Custom parameter name on the target COMP, e.g. 'Speed'.

channel.description: Source channel to drive it, e.g. 'bass'.

add_master.description: Append a 'Reactivity' master float knob (0-2, default = intensity) on the target COMP that scales every binding.

tools.name: create_replicator
tools.description: Wire a Replicator COMP that clones a template COMP once per row of a Table DAT — TouchDesigner's idiomatic 'N copies from data' mechanism (menus, scoreboards, per-track decks, instanced panels). Resolves or creates the template COMP (omit template_path → a minimal container with a Text) and the driving Table DAT (omit table_path → a small example table; `rows` sets how many demo rows), creates the replicator under parent_path, points its driving-table and master parameters at them, sets the replication method to 'by table', and optionally drops an onReplicate callback DAT stub for per-clone setup. The Replicator's parameter names vary by TD build, so each is set probe-first and the report includes which parameter took plus the live parameter list. Then it pulses a re-replicate so the clones appear. Re-replicating is destructive to previously generated clones, which the replicator deletes and re-creates on cook.

parent_path.description: COMP to build the replicator inside.

template_path.description: Existing COMP to clone per row. Omit → create a minimal template COMP (a container with a Text).

table_path.description: Table DAT whose rows drive the clones. Omit → create a small example Table DAT.

rows.description: When creating an example table, how many example rows (0 = a 3-row demo).

callback_stub.description: Generate an onReplicate callback DAT stub (per-clone setup hook).

tools.name: create_data_reactive
tools.description: Wire arbitrary external data (weather, follower count, sensor readings, OSC values) onto a COMP's custom numeric parameters — the data counterpart to bind_audio_reactive. Point `target` at a COMP with numeric custom-parameter knobs, `source_chop` at a live-data CHOP (e.g. a create_data_source Null), and provide explicit `mappings` (data channel → param name) each with an input range [in_min, in_max] and output range [out_min, out_max] so the data is correctly re-mapped to the parameter's visual range. Set `smooth` > 0 to insert a Lag CHOP (symmetric attack+release) so noisy or jittery data does not flicker the visuals. Fail-forward: a missing source CHOP or absent channel are warnings — only a missing/non-COMP target is fatal. Build the data CHOP first with create_data_source; use bind_to_channel for finer single-parameter control.

target.description: COMP whose numeric custom parameters should react to the data.

source_chop.description: CHOP carrying the live data channels (e.g. a create_data_source Null). Channels can be weather values, follower counts, sensor readings, etc.

param.description: Target custom-parameter name on the COMP, e.g. 'Speed'.

channel.description: Source CHOP channel to drive it, e.g. 'temperature'.

in_min.description: Input range min (data value). Data is rarely 0–1, set this to the expected minimum.

in_max.description: Input range max (data value). Set this to the expected maximum of the data channel.

mappings.description: Explicit data→param mappings with per-mapping range remap. Data is rarely 0–1, so set in_min/in_max to the real data range for correct visual mapping.

smooth.description: Symmetric smoothing in seconds (Lag CHOP) applied to all channels so noisy data does not jitter visuals. 0 = no smoothing.

tools.name: create_beat_grid_sequencer
tools.description: Build a programmable step-grid sequencer driven by a Beat CHOP on the global TD tempo: a Table DAT holds the per-step pattern (values or 1/0 flags), and a CHOP Execute DAT fires on every beat boundary, reads the current step (count % steps) from the table, and dispatches — action=param sets a custom parameter to the step value; action=cue recalls the cue for active steps (cues stored with manage_cue). The deterministic, repeating-rhythm instrument between create_autopilot (random drift) and create_cue_sequencer (linear list): program a strobe on beats 1+3, a hue shift on the bar, etc. Reprogramme the grid live by editing the step_table DAT. NOTE: beat-callback timing is UNVERIFIED offline — check op().time.play if steps don't fire when the TD timeline is paused.

parent_path.description: Parent COMP path to create the sequencer inside.

target.description: COMP whose parameter or cue each active step fires on a beat boundary.

steps.description: Number of steps in the grid (e.g. 16 = one bar of 16th notes at 4/4).

action.description: param: set a target custom-parameter value per active step; cue: recall a named cue per active step (cues stored with manage_cue).

param.description: (action=param) The custom-parameter name on the target COMP to set on each active step.

pattern.description: Per-step values (action=param) or 1/0 active flags (action=cue); length should match 'steps'. Omit to auto-generate an example pattern.

bpm_source.description: Path to an existing Beat CHOP or tempo source. Omit to create a new Beat CHOP (on the global TD tempo).

tools.name: rebuild_network
tools.description: Reconstruct a live network inside a COMP from a serialize_network spec — the REBUILD half of a git-diffable round-trip. Takes a JSON spec of nodes (name, operator type, parameters as constants/expressions/binds, inbound wires by name, optional x/y) and, in one pass, creates every node, applies its parameters and expressions, then wires inputs by resolving each `from` reference to the freshly created node. Caller expression/bind source requires TDMCP_RAW_PYTHON=on; constant-only specs remain allowed by the MCP caller-code policy. This tool's one-pass reconstruction still uses /api/exec, so every mode requires TDMCP_BRIDGE_ALLOW_EXEC=1. Fail-forward: an unknown operator type, missing parameter, or unresolved wire becomes a warning and the rest still build, so a partial reconstruction still returns useful results. Set clear_existing to delete the parent's current children first (destructive). Set auto_layout to auto-position every node by dependency (longest-path columns, left→right) from the spec's inputs graph, overriding any manual x/y. Returns the created node names, wire count, parameters set, and any warnings.

parent_path.description: COMP to rebuild the network inside.

root.description: Original root path the spec was serialized from (informational only).

name.description: Name for the node inside the parent (TD may adjust it to avoid collisions).

params.description: Map of parameter name → { value | mode | expr } to apply after creation.

value.description: Constant value for the parameter (used when mode is constant or omitted).

mode.description: Parameter mode: 'EXPRESSION', 'BIND', or 'CONSTANT' (case-insensitive). Omit for a plain constant.

expr.description: Expression or bind string, required when mode is EXPRESSION or BIND, e.g. 'me.time.seconds'.

inputs.description: Inbound wires for this node, each referencing another node by `from` name.

from.description: Name of an earlier node in this spec to wire from.

out_index.description: Output connector index on the source node (default 0).

in_index.description: Input connector index on this node (default 0).

x.description: Optional node X position (nodeX) in the network editor.

y.description: Optional node Y position (nodeY) in the network editor.

nodes.description: Nodes to create, parameterize, and wire, in order.

clear_existing.description: Delete existing children of parent_path first (destructive).

auto_layout.description: Auto-position every node by dependency (longest-path columns, left→right) from the spec's `inputs` graph, overriding any per-node x/y. False (default) honors manual x/y only.

tools.name: create_envelope_follower
tools.description: EXPERIMENTAL — Build a reactive signal-shaping chain (attack/release envelope + threshold gate or sidechain ducking) from a CHOP channel, for 'pump the whole layer on every kick' or similar sidechain effects. Creates a container with: a Select CHOP isolating the source channel by absolute path (no cross-container wire), a Lag CHOP shaping the attack/release envelope, a Logic+Math CHOP threshold gate (gate mode: silence the output below threshold) or an inverted Math CHOP (duck mode: output dips to 0 on a hit, rises on silence — classic sidechain pumping), and a Null CHOP as the stable output handle. Optionally binds the shaped output to target parameters by expression. The gate threshold uses a Logic CHOP whose par names (convert/boundmin/boundmax) match detect_onsets — but these are UNVERIFIED across TD builds; gate reads near 0 at the 0.2 default with most sources — tune threshold live. Use bind_to_channel with attack/release for a simpler Lag-only envelope without a gate.

parent_path.description: Where to build the follower chain (a COMP path, e.g. '/project1').

name.description: Base name for the container COMP that holds the chain.

source_chop.description: Path of the CHOP carrying the trigger channel (e.g. '/project1/audio/features' or an onset Null).

channel.description: Channel name to follow from source_chop (e.g. 'bass', 'kick', 'level'). The Select CHOP isolates it by name.

attack.description: Envelope rise time in seconds — how quickly the output climbs after a hit (fast = punchy, e.g. 0.001–0.05).

release.description: Envelope fall time in seconds — how slowly the output decays after the signal drops (slow = smooth tail, e.g. 0.1–0.8).

threshold.description: Gate threshold [0–1]. Below this level the output is silenced (gate) or held at 1 (duck). Start low (0.05–0.2) and raise if false triggers occur. NOTE: gate thresholding uses a Logic CHOP whose par names may vary by TD build — EXPERIMENTAL.

mode.description: gate: pass the shaped envelope only while it is above threshold — silences the output when the signal is quiet. duck: sidechain/ducking — the output dips toward 0 on every hit and returns to 1 on silence (inverted gate, classic pumping compressor feel).

targets.description: Optional list of 'nodePath.parName' targets to bind to the shaped envelope output by expression. Omit to just build the chain (the Null CHOP output can be bound later with bind_to_channel).

tools.name: create_midi_map
tools.description: HARDWARE-GATED SCAFFOLD. Build a MIDI controller preset for a supported device (apc_mini / launchpad / midi_mix / nanokontrol / generic): creates a midiinCHOP + a labeled bind Table DAT, and optionally auto-binds faders/knobs to a target COMP's numeric custom parameters. Explicit bindings can override or supplement the preset. CC/note numbers are best-effort from published MIDI charts and MUST be validated with real hardware — actual assignments depend on device firmware. This tool is HELD FROM RELEASE until hardware validation is complete. For one-at-a-time MIDI learn of a single control, use learn_control instead.

parent_path.description: COMP to create the MIDI map inside.

name.description: Name for the MIDI In CHOP node created under parent_path.

device.description: Controller preset. Each preset embeds a best-effort CC/note map for that device (UNVERIFIED — real numbers depend on firmware; validate with hardware). 'generic' builds a bare MIDI In + a template bind table with no preset.

target.description: COMP whose custom numeric params/cues the preset auto-binds faders/knobs onto. Faders bind to the first N float/int custom pars; pads look for matching cues. Auto-binding is best-effort and hardware-gated.

bindings.description: Explicit control→param/cue overrides. Applied after the preset auto-map. Omit to rely entirely on the device preset's default map.

control.description: Control id from the device preset map, e.g. 'fader1', 'knob3', 'pad5'. For 'generic' device, use any label you choose.

cue.description: Cue name to recall when this pad is triggered.

tools.name: create_modulators
tools.description: Build a bank of N BPM-synced LFOs in one self-contained container — each an oscillator (sine/triangle/saw/square or a random sample-&-hold) with its own rate-in-beats, output range and phase offset. Every rate locks to a tempo source (a create_tempo_sync Null, or TouchDesigner's global tempo) by expression, so the whole bank speeds up/slows down with the music and stays phase-continuous across tempo changes. All outputs land on one Null CHOP (mod_out) with one named channel per modulator, ready for bind_to_channel — the 'everything breathes' lever. Note: modulators are timeline-driven, so they only move while the timeline is playing. Re-running with an existing container name rebuilds it in place (clearing that container's children), so this tool is marked destructive and hidden from the safe profile.

name.description: Name of the self-contained modulator-bank container.

parent_path.description: Parent COMP the 'modulators' container is created inside.

name.description: Output channel name for this modulator (e.g. 'breathe', 'sweep'). Sanitized to a valid channel name; defaults to mod1, mod2, …

shape.description: Oscillator shape. 'saw' is a rising ramp; 'random' is a sample-&-hold (a new random value held each cycle) built from a Noise CHOP. Every shape sweeps the full depth range.

rate_beats.description: Cycle length in BEATS — how many beats one full cycle takes. 4 = one cycle per bar (slow breathe), 1 = one cycle per beat, 0.5 = twice per beat (eighths). Locked to the tempo source so it tracks BPM.

depth_min.description: Low end of this modulator's output range.

depth_max.description: High end of this modulator's output range.

phase.description: Phase offset 0–1 (fraction of a cycle). Use to fan a bank out of step (e.g. 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75).

modulators.description: The modulators (LFOs) to build. Each becomes one named output channel on the bank's Null.

tempo_source.description: Path to an existing tempo Null/Beat CHOP carrying a 'bpm' channel (e.g. the Null from create_tempo_sync, '/project1/tempo_sync/tempo'). Omit to create a fresh Beat CHOP locked to TouchDesigner's global tempo inside the bank.

bpm_channel.description: Name of the BPM channel on the tempo source to lock rates to.

expose_controls.description: Expose a live custom-parameter page on the bank: a master Rate multiplier and a master Depth (amplitude) scale, so you can speed up or flatten the whole bank from one knob during a show.

tools.name: create_look_bank
tools.description: A playable snapshot row: store N named 'looks' (snapshots of a control COMP's numeric/toggle/menu parameters) in a visible, editable Table DAT, with one momentary recall button per slot (snap or crossfade) plus a master A↔B morph knob that blends continuously between two chosen looks. Reuses manage_cue's morph engine (so a recall behaves exactly like a cue morph, with optional beat/bar quantize) and mirrors slots into the COMP's cues so they interoperate with manage_cue / create_control_surface. Pulses and strings are always skipped at capture. Build cues/params with create_control_panel first.

action.description: build: create the look-bank container (Table DAT + A↔B morph knob + recall button row) on a control COMP. store: snapshot the COMP's current numeric look into a named slot. recall: jump or crossfade to a slot. set_ab: assign which two slots the A↔B knob blends, and optionally set the knob. list / delete slots.

comp_path.description: Control COMP whose custom-parameter values the looks capture (a control-panel container, e.g. from create_control_panel). The look-bank widgets are built inside it; recall drives this COMP's params.

name.description: Name of the look-bank panel container built inside comp_path.

slot.description: Slot name (required for store / recall / delete).

morph_seconds.description: (recall) 0 = snap instantly; >0 = crossfade to the slot over this many seconds (eased), via the cue morph engine.

quantize.description: (recall) Defer the snap/crossfade to the next musical boundary (project tempo), so look changes land on the downbeat. Mirrors manage_cue.

slot_a.description: (set_ab) Slot the A↔B knob reads at value 0.

slot_b.description: (set_ab) Slot the A↔B knob reads at value 1.

ab.description: (set_ab) Optionally set the A↔B knob position now (0 = slot A, 1 = slot B, 0.5 = halfway). Omit to just (re)assign the slots.

include.description: (store) Restrict the snapshot to these custom-parameter names. Omit to capture every numeric/toggle/menu parameter (pulses and strings are always skipped).

tools.name: create_sidechain_pump
tools.description: EXPERIMENTAL — One-call 'pump the whole rig on the kick': build a sidechain ducking envelope from a trigger CHOP channel and bind multiple target parameters to dip on every hit. Distinct from create_envelope_follower (which builds the chain + optional gate/duck mode with a threshold); this tool is the ergonomic multi-target pump with a single depth knob and a rest_value anchor — ideal for classic pumping compressor feel across many targets at once. Builds a container with: a Select CHOP isolating the source channel by absolute path (no cross-container wires), a Lag CHOP shaping attack/release, a Limit CHOP clamping to [0,1] (type=clamp/min/max, live-validated on TD 099 — guarded with warnings), and a Null CHOP 'pump' as the stable output handle. Each target gets the expression: rest_value * (1 - depth * op('<pump>')[chan0]). Per-target failures become warnings; fatal only if source_chop or parent COMP is missing.

parent_path.description: Parent COMP path where the sidechain pump container is created (e.g. '/project1').

name.description: Base name for the container COMP that holds the pump chain.

source_chop.description: Path of the trigger CHOP (e.g. an onset Null, kick-level CHOP, or audio feature output). This is the signal that drives the pump — high = dip.

channel.description: Channel name to follow from source_chop (e.g. 'level', 'kick', 'bass'). The Select CHOP isolates it by name.

targets.description: List of 'nodePath.parName' pairs to bind to the pump output by expression. Each target dips toward rest*(1-depth) on a hit and returns to rest_value on silence. Omit to build the chain only (bind manually with bind_to_channel later).

depth.description: How hard the pump dips on a trigger hit [0–1]. 0 = no dip (targets stay at rest_value), 1 = full dip to zero. 0.7–0.9 is typical for a strong pumping compressor feel.

attack.description: Envelope rise time in seconds — how quickly the pump signal climbs after a hit (controls how snappy the initial dip is). Typical: 0.001–0.02.

release.description: Envelope fall time in seconds — how slowly the pump returns to silence after the trigger drops. Controls the 'pumping tail'. Typical: 0.1–0.6.

rest_value.description: The target parameter value at silence (no trigger). On a hit, the expression drives the target toward rest_value*(1-depth). Default 1.0 works for opacity/gain/level parameters.

tools.name: create_band_router
tools.description: Split an audio signal into EQ bands and route each band to its own target parameter(s) — the musician-friendly 'bass -> this, highs -> that' patch. Builds a container with: a Select CHOP isolating the source audio by absolute path (no cross-container wire), N audiofilterCHOP band-pass slices tiling the spectrum in log-frequency space (the same audioFilter idiom extract_audio_features uses), an Analyze CHOP per band measuring its level via rmspower, a Merge + Lag smoothing the per-band envelope (release in seconds), and a Null 'bands_out' carrying one channel per band named band0..bandN-1 (band0 = lowest). Each target route binds a band's smoothed level to a parameter by expression (op('<bands_out>')['band<i>'] * scale + offset). The bands_out Null is also directly bind_to_channel-able for routes you add later. EXTENSION sibling of extract_audio_features (that one extracts named features; this one is the band-split + multi-target router). NOTE: the analyze 'rmspower' function value and the channel-rename pars are UNVERIFIED across TD builds — they are set in guarded tries with fallbacks (abs envelope / upstream channel names), and a single audiospectrumCHOP is the fallback if audiofilterCHOP is unavailable; per-item failures surface as warnings rather than failing the build.

parent_path.description: Where to build the band-router container (a COMP path, e.g. '/project1').

name.description: Base name for the container COMP that holds the EQ split + router.

source_chop.description: Path of the raw audio CHOP to split (e.g. an Audio Device In or Audio File In, '/project1/audiodevin1'). REQUIRED.

bands.description: Number of EQ bands to split the signal into (e.g. 4 = sub / low / mid / high). The output Null carries one channel per band, named band0..bandN-1 (band0 = lowest).

targets.description: Optional band->parameter routes. Each binds one band's smoothed level to a parameter by expression (op('<bands_out>')['band<i>'] * scale + offset). Omit to just build the split (bind later with bind_to_channel against the bands_out Null).

band.description: Band index to read from (0 = lowest band, bands-1 = highest).

offset.description: Add to the scaled value (mapping offset).

smooth.description: Release/lag time in seconds applied to every band level — smooths the per-band envelope so reactivity follows a clean curve instead of flickering on raw audio (e.g. 0.05 punchy, 0.2 smooth).

tools.name: create_xy_pad
tools.description: Build a draggable 2D (XY) gesture pad — a Container COMP whose pointer drag drives an x/y CHOP of normalized control channels, optionally remapped into ranges and bound by expression to target parameters (e.g. an effect's two main knobs). Add a 3rd (Z) axis via z_target to also get a slider. Open the container in Perform/Panel mode and drag inside it to scrub X/Y live. The pad reads its drag through a Panel CHOP; the u/v drag-channel names are probed at build time (they vary by TD build) and any mismatch is reported as a warning. Leave the axis targets empty to just expose the x/y channels and bind them later with bind_to_channel.

parent_path.description: COMP path that will hold the XY pad (e.g. '/project1').

name.description: Name of the container COMP built as the draggable pad.

x_target.description: Optional 'nodePath.parName' driven by the X axis. Empty = just expose the x/y channels (bind later with bind_to_channel).

y_target.description: Optional 'nodePath.parName' driven by the Y axis. Empty = none.

z_target.description: Optional 'nodePath.parName' driven by a 3rd (Z) axis. When set, a slider is added (the pad has no native 3rd axis) and its value0 drives this target.

x_range.description: Output range [low, high] for X. The pad's normalized u (0..1) is remapped into it.

y_range.description: Output range [low, high] for Y. The pad's normalized v (0..1) is remapped into it.

z_range.description: Output range [low, high] for the optional Z slider (0..1 remapped into it).

label_x.description: Display label for the X axis (used in the summary).

label_y.description: Display label for the Y axis (used in the summary).

size.description: Pad size in pixels (square: width = height = size).

tools.name: create_time_echo
tools.description: EXPERIMENTAL — Apply a per-pixel time effect to a source TOP: echo trails, slit-scan, or per-pixel time displacement (the 'time machine' melt/slice look). Builds a container COMP that selects the source by absolute path (no cross-container wire) and then, by mode: echo — a feedbackTOP (wired input + forced resolution so the loop is not black) blended over the live frame at opacity=feedback to leave fading ghost trails; slit_scan — a cacheTOP buffering `frames` and a time-machine TOP reading different rows from different points in time; time_displace — the same cache read back through a luminance gradient (`displace_top` or a built-in vertical ramp) so bright pixels show older frames. The time-machine read operator is PROBED LIVE (timeMachineTOP → cacheSelectTOP fallback) because the optype name varies by TD build; the feedback opacity par (opacity → fadeval) and cache-depth par (cachesize → maxframes) are also set defensively. Every par/connect failure is collected as a warning and the chain still returns its output Null — UNVERIFIED across TD builds; tune live. Ends with a Null TOP 'out'.

parent_path.description: Where to build the time-echo chain (a COMP path, e.g. '/project1').

name.description: Base name for the container COMP that holds the chain.
